page: Google Cloud Platform n1-highcpu-4 is a compute-optimized virtual machine instance belonging to the N1 machine family. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 2 physical cores of an Intel Xeon processor running at 2.3 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The instance is configured with 4.0 GB of system memory, yielding a low memory-to-vCPU ratio of approximately 0.9 GB per core. It does not include local NVMe storage or GPU accelerators, relying entirely on network-attached storage.

Benchmark evaluations place the n1-highcpu-4 in the lower performance tiers. In stress-ng testing, the instance achieved a single-core score of 1125.48 and a multi-core score of 2941.66, both categorized as weak. Memory bandwidth tests show 162.49 GB/sec for cached small blocks and 25.58 GB/sec for uncached large blocks. Geekbench testing reports a single-core score of 926.0 and a multi-core score of 1979.0, reflecting poor to weak performance across image processing, text processing, and software compilation tasks.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the n1-highcpu-4 offers a budget-friendly entry point for compute-focused workloads that do not require substantial memory footprints. However, the older Intel Xeon architecture and weak benchmark results present a tradeoff in raw processing speed compared to newer instance generations. This instance is best suited for lightweight, CPU-bound tasks such as basic web serving, simple database operations, and minor text or data processing pipelines that can operate within the 4.0 GB memory constraint.
